chunks: Hadith 4527: “Indeed, Ibrāhīm, the Friend of the Most Merciful, peace be upon him, complained to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, about the temperament of Sārah. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: ‘The likeness of a woman is the likeness of a rib: if you straighten it, it will break; and if you leave it, you will enjoy benefit from it.’”
I said, “Who said this?” So he became angry, then said: “By Allah, this is the saying of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family.”

key_terms.إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Ibrāhīm, the prophet mentioned in the narration
key_terms.الضِّلْعِ: rib, the metaphor used in the hadith
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: woman, in the parable being cited
key_terms.انْكَسَرَ: it broke, describing the result of trying to straighten it
key_terms.خَلِيلَ الرَّحْمَنِ: the intimate friend of the Most Merciful
key_terms.سَارَةَ: Sārah, the wife of Ibrāhīm عليه السلام
key_terms.قَوْلُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the statement of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith about woman being like a rib mean in the context of spousal relations?
ai.summary: This hadith relates that Ibrāhīm عليه السلام complained about Sārah’s temperament, and Allah عَزَّ وَجَلَّ revealed a parable comparing woman to a rib. It concludes by affirming, with emphasis, that this wording is from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, highlighting its authority as a prophetic tradition in the context of spousal relations.
